study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
exposure: Postpartum time points (7 weeks and 8 months)
cohort: The study included primiparous women who underwent pelvic MRI and clinical examinations at 7 weeks and 8 months after vaginal delivery.
finding: After vaginal delivery, most women (70%) showed a "recovery" of level III pelvic support by 8 months postpartum, characterized by smaller UGH, LH, and LA measurements and a more ventrally oriented levator plate shape; however, nearly 30% had larger level III measurements and a more dorsally oriented levator plate shape, indicating "impaired recovery" of support.
mod_finding: The study specifically quantified changes in pelvic support measurements and levator plate shape at 7 weeks and 8 months following vaginal delivery, identifying that while most women showed recovery, a significant minority experienced impaired recovery.
